source_snapshot.title: feat(mcp): serve Ix's tools over MCP as `ix mcp`
source_snapshot.body:
Closes #219.

Serves Ix's graph tools over MCP from the CLI itself, so a host talks to `ix mcp`
instead of to one of six separately-maintained plugin servers.

## What this adds

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `ix mcp` | Serves the tools over stdio |
| `ix mcp install` | Registers that server with the AI clients on the machine |
| `ix mcp doctor` | Reports what each client currently points at |

Seven hosts are covered: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI,
OpenClaw and opencode.

Commands run **in-process**, not by shelling back out to `ix` — one CLI startup
per server, not one per tool call.

## Why it is a superset

The six plugins never shared one tool surface, so delegating to `ix mcp` as it
first stood would have *removed* tools from three of them:

| Plugin | Tools | Not served before this |
|---|---:|---|
| codex, cursor | 23 | — |
| gemini | 23 | `ix_decide`, `ix_ingest`, `ix_query`, `ix_status` |
| openclaw, opencode | 17 | + `ix_docs_tool`, `ix_neighbors` |
| claude | 0 (skills only) | — |

`ix_decide` and `ix_ingest` were real gaps and are now served. Three exclusions
are deliberate: `ix_query` is the deprecated command our own docs tell agents not
to use; `ix_neighbors` and `ix_docs_tool` are composites of tools served
individually. `ix_status` is gemini's name for `ix_health`.

Pro tools are advertised only when `@ix/pro` resolves. `ix_briefing` and
`ix_decisions` were previously offered to every install while answering "requires
Ix Pro" on every call — which an agent cannot tell apart from a real failure.
OSS installs see 22 tools, Pro 25.

## install never overwrites

The six plugins register their own server under the same `ix-memory` name, so a
name held by anything that is not `ix mcp` is reported and left alone. `--force`
replaces, `--host` narrows, `--dry-run` writes nothing. A registration that
cannot be read is treated as occupied rather than free — guessing "free" is the
one wrong guess that destroys someone's config.

Writes go through each client's own MCP command where one exists (`claude`/
`codex`/`gemini mcp add`, `openclaw mcp set`, `code --add-mcp`), so the client
owns its config format. Only Cursor (no MCP CLI) and opencode (`opencode mcp add`
is interactive) are written directly — JSON, merged in place, every existing key
preserved, `.bak` kept, and a file that does not parse is refused.

Two detection bugs found against real installs are fixed: Gemini prints its
listing to stderr behind ~28 extension-loader errors, several naming the
extension `ix-memory` — matching the first line containing the name reported a
diagnostic as the registration. And `openclaw mcp show` pretty-prints JSON across
lines, so line-at-a-time matching read our own entry as a stranger's and raised a
false conflict on every re-run.

## Windows

`install` wrote `command: "ix"` for all seven hosts. npm ships no `ix.exe`, only
`ix.CMD`, and a host spawning the bare name through CreateProcess never consults
PATHEXT — so the registration resolved to nothing however well-formed the rest
was. ix-codex-plugin already hit this (its #13); consolidating would have
discarded that fix and handed the problem to every host. The launcher is now
resolved once here and each host records what `where ix` returned. Unix keeps the
bare name, which survives an upgrade that moves the install.

## Testing

798 → **800 tests pass** (59 files), lint clean, build clean. 648 lines of new
tests across `mcp.test.ts`, `mcp-install.test.ts` and `mcp-runner.test.ts`.

Driven end-to-end through a real MCP client. `ix mcp install` was run for real
against cursor, opencode and openclaw and then fully reverted; **the other four
hosts are dry-run only**, and the Windows launcher path is untested on Windows
from this machine — the Unix path is unchanged and resolution falls back to the
bare name.

## What this unblocks

`docs/mcp-plugin-consolidation.md` records the migration order. Two plugin PRs
are already open, green, and gated on `ix >= 0.9.3`:
ix-codex-plugin#24 and ix-cursor-plugin#24 — both lossless.

MCP absorbs the ~15.3k-line tool layer. It has no concept of a hook, skill or
slash command, so ~10.6k lines of agents/hooks/skills stay host-specific and the
plugins do not go away.

+### Use Ix from any MCP client
+
+The CLI includes a canonical stdio MCP server with the same graph tools used by
+the editor integrations:
+
+```bash
+ix mcp
+```
+
+To register it with every AI client on the machine at once:
+
+```bash
+ix mcp install            # detect clients and register `ix mcp` with each
+ix mcp install --dry-run  # show what would change, write nothing
+ix mcp doctor             # check each client's registration
+```
+
+`install` knows Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw and
+opencode. It writes through each client's own MCP command where one exists
+(`claude mcp add`, `codex mcp add`, `gemini mcp add`, `openclaw mcp set`,
+`code --add-mcp`), so the client owns its config format; only Cursor and
+opencode are edited directly, and both are merged in place with a `.bak` kept
+alongside.
+
+**It never overwrites.** If the name `ix-memory` already belongs to a different
+server — an earlier Ix plugin, say — that client is reported and left exactly as
+it was. Pass `--force` to replace it, or `--host <id>` to limit the run.
+
+To register a single client by hand instead, point it at `ix` with the argument
+`mcp`. For Codex:
+
+```bash
+codex mcp add ix-memory -- ix mcp
+```
+
+The client launches the server in the active workspace, so every Ix tool uses
+that repository's graph and configuration.
+
+Tool calls run inside the server process. Set `IX_MCP_SUBPROCESS=1` to run each
+one as a separate `ix` child process instead — slower by roughly the CLI's
+startup time per call, but fully isolated.

@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+# Consolidating the per-host plugins onto `ix mcp`
+
+Ix ships six per-host plugin repos, each with its own tool implementation:
+`ix-claude-plugin`, `ix-codex-plugin`, `ix-cursor-plugin`, `ix-gemini-plugin`,
+`ix-openclaw-plugin`, `ix-opencode-plugin`. `ix mcp` serves the same graph tools
+from the CLI, so those implementations can be retired in favour of one server.
+
+This is what that costs and in what order it can happen.
+
+## What MCP can and cannot absorb
+
+Measured across the six repos (source only, excluding `node_modules` and `dist`):
+
+| Layer | Lines | Absorbed by `ix mcp`? |
+|---|---:|---|
+| Tool implementations (`mcp/`, `tools/`, `runtime/`) | ~15,300 | **Yes** |
+| Agents, hooks, skills, commands, rules | ~10,600 | **No** |
+
+MCP standardizes tools, resources and prompts. It has no concept of a hook, a
+skill, a slash command or a host instruction file, so roughly 40% of what the
+plugins do has no MCP equivalent and stays host-specific whatever else happens.
+Consolidation retires the tool layer; it does not retire the plugins.
+
+## Tool-surface parity
+
+The plugins never shared one tool surface. Measured against `ix mcp`:
+
+| Plugin | Tools | Tools `ix mcp` lacked |
+|---|---:|---|
+| ix-codex-plugin | 23 | — |
+| ix-cursor-plugin | 23 | — |
+| ix-gemini-plugin | 23 | `ix_decide`, `ix_ingest`, `ix_query`, `ix_status` |
+| ix-openclaw-plugin | 17 | `ix_decide`, `ix_docs_tool`, `ix_ingest`, `ix_neighbors`, `ix_query` |
+| ix-opencode-plugin | 17 | `ix_decide`, `ix_docs_tool`, `ix_ingest`, `ix_neighbors`, `ix_query` |
+| ix-claude-plugin | 0 (skills only) | — |
+
+`ix mcp` now closes that gap, with three deliberate exclusions:
+
+- **`ix_query`** — the deprecated command the CLI docs tell agents not to use
+  ("produces oversized low-signal responses"). Dropped on purpose.
+- **`ix_neighbors`** — a composite of `ix_callers` + `ix_callees` + `ix_depends`,
+  all served individually. Callers lose one round-trip, not a capability.
+- **`ix_docs_tool`** — a composite over `ix_overview`, likewise served.
+
+And `ix_status` is Gemini's name for what `ix mcp` calls `ix_health`; both run
+`ix status`.
+
+`ix_decide` and `ix_ingest` were real gaps and are now served. `ix_decide` is a
+write and needs Pro, so it is advertised only when `@ix/pro` resolves — as are
+`ix_briefing` and `ix_decisions`, which this server previously offered to every
+install even though every call answered "requires Ix Pro".
+
+**Net:** codex and cursor can delegate with no change in what an agent can do.
+gemini, openclaw and opencode lose only `ix_query` and the two composites.
+
+## Order of work
+
+1. **Ship `ix mcp` in a released `@ix/cli`.** Nothing downstream can depend on it
+   until then. The plugins already gate features on CLI version floors, so this
+   becomes a new floor.
+2. **Point each plugin's registration at `ix mcp`** instead of its own server,
+   and delete that server. Start with codex and cursor — those two are lossless.
+3. **Leave agents, hooks, skills and commands where they are.** They are the
+   plugins' remaining reason to exist.
+
+Step 2 is one PR per repo and each is independently revertible; a plugin that has
+not migrated keeps working, because `ix mcp install` refuses to take a name that
+another server already holds.

feat(mcp): serve Ix tools over MCP, executing commands in-process

Adds `ix mcp`, a stdio MCP server exposing 23 graph tools, so any
MCP-capable client can drive Ix. Each host still needs its own
registration; for Codex that is `codex mcp add ix-memory -- ix mcp`.

Tool calls run inside the server process rather than spawning the CLI per
call. Booting main.js costs ~0.58s before any query runs, which an agent
pays on every hop of a locate -> callers -> read chain; measured end to
end over stdio, eight tool calls drop from 8502ms to 1282ms. It also lets
resolve.ts's per-cwd scope cache survive between calls. Running commands
in the server's own process needs three things the child process gave for
free:

- `ix status` and `ix text` call process.exit(1) on their error paths.
  In a child that ends one command; here it would take the whole server
  down mid-session, so process.exit becomes a throw the runner turns into
  a failed tool result.
- Runs are serialized. Commands report failure via process.exitCode,
  which is a non-configurable property on Node 22 and so cannot be made
  context-local; isolating output per async context while the exit code
  stayed global would attribute a call's output to the right result and
  its success to the wrong one. This costs nothing measurable — three
  concurrent calls as child processes took 1304/1733/1888ms competing for
  Node boots, versus 15/250/251ms serialized in-process.
- The transport writes JSON-RPC through its own handle on fd 1, and
  output that cannot be attributed to a run goes to stderr, so a command
  outliving its timeout cannot desync the protocol. AsyncLocalStorage
  keeps such an orphan's late output out of the next call's result.

The command tree is rebuilt per run because commander does not clear
parsed option values between parses, which would leak --path from one
ix_text call into the next one that omitted it.

IX_MCP_SUBPROCESS=1 restores the isolated child-process behaviour.

feat(mcp): add `ix mcp install` and `ix mcp doctor`

Registers `ix mcp` with the AI clients present on the machine, and reports
what each one currently points at. Covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
VS Code, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw and opencode.

Writes go through each client's own MCP command wherever one exists
(claude/codex/gemini `mcp add`, `openclaw mcp set`, `code --add-mcp`), so
the client owns its config format and an upstream format change cannot
corrupt a file here. Only Cursor (no MCP CLI) and opencode (`opencode mcp
add` is interactive and takes no arguments) are written directly; both are
JSON, merged in place with every existing key preserved and a `.bak` kept.
A config that does not parse is refused rather than replaced.

install never overwrites. Ix already ships six per-host plugins that
register their own server under the same name — `ix-memory` currently
resolves to `python3 .../server.py` on Codex and a Gemini extension's
`node dist/server.js` on this machine — so a name held by anything that is
not `ix mcp` is reported and left alone. --force replaces it, --host
narrows the run, --dry-run writes nothing. A registration that cannot be
read is treated as occupied, not free: guessing "free" is the one wrong
guess that destroys someone's config.

Two things detection has to get right, both found against real installs:

- Gemini prints its listing to stderr behind ~28 extension-loader errors,
  several naming the extension, which is itself called ix-memory. Matching
  the first line containing the name reports a diagnostic as the
  registration, so obvious log lines are skipped.
- `openclaw mcp list` prints names only, and `openclaw mcp show`
  pretty-prints JSON across lines, putting "ix" and "mcp" on different
  ones. Line-at-a-time matching read our own entry as a stranger's and
  raised a false conflict on every re-run; definitions are now classified
  whole.

doctor additionally checks that the bare command `ix` resolves on PATH,
since that is what every registration launches.

feat(mcp): make ix mcp a superset of the per-host plugin tools

Prerequisite for retiring the six plugins' own tool implementations. The
plugins never shared one tool surface, so delegating to `ix mcp` as it
stood would have removed tools from three of them:

  codex, cursor    23 tools, identical — lossless today
  gemini           23, of which decide/ingest/query/status were not served
  openclaw         17, of which decide/docs_tool/ingest/neighbors/query
  opencode         17, same as openclaw
  claude            0 — skills only, nothing to migrate

`ix_decide` and `ix_ingest` were the only real capability gaps and are now
served. Three exclusions are deliberate: `ix_query` is the deprecated
command the CLI docs tell agents not to use; `ix_neighbors` and
`ix_docs_tool` are composites of callers/callees/depends and of overview,
all served individually. `ix_status` is gemini's name for `ix_health`.

Pro tools are now advertised only when @ix/pro actually resolves.
`ix_briefing` and `ix_decisions` were offered to every install while
answering "requires Ix Pro" on every call, which an agent cannot tell
apart from a real failure; `ix_decide` would have been a third. OSS
installs see 22 tools, Pro installs 25 — both observed on one machine,
since the global @ix/pro resolves for the CLI but not under vitest.

`ix mcp doctor` reports the count this install actually advertises rather
than the theoretical maximum.

docs/mcp-plugin-consolidation.md records what MCP can absorb (~15.3k lines
of tool implementations) and what it cannot (~10.6k lines of agents, hooks,
skills and commands, which have no MCP equivalent and stay host-specific),
plus the order the migration has to happen in.

fix(mcp): register the resolved ix launcher on Windows

`ix mcp install` wrote `command: "ix"` into all seven hosts. npm ships no
`ix.exe` — only `ix.CMD` — and a host that spawns the bare name through
CreateProcess never consults PATHEXT, so the registration resolves to
nothing on Windows however well-formed the rest of it is.

ix-codex-plugin already hit this and resolves the path itself before
spawning (its #13). Consolidating onto `ix mcp` would have discarded that
fix and handed the same problem to every host, so the launcher is resolved
once here and each host records what `where ix` returned. Unix keeps the
bare name, which survives an upgrade that moves the install.

Untested on Windows from this machine; the Unix path is unchanged and
resolution falls back to the bare name.

fix(mcp): stop exporting six symbols nothing imports

The dead-code gate (knip) rejected the branch. `resolveLauncher`,
`cursorConfigPath`, `opencodeConfigPath` and `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` are used
only inside their own module, and server.ts re-exported `runCurrentIx`
and `IxRunResult`, which no caller takes from there — tests import
`runCurrentIx` from runner.js directly. Only `IxRunner` is genuinely
consumed through server.js, so the re-export narrows to that.

Lint passes locally either way; knip is the check that catches this, and
it does not run as part of `npm run lint`.

fix(mcp): close the config-write file-system race

CodeQL js/file-system-race, high, on the PR. writeJsonConfig checked
existsSync and then read, copied and wrote — the check could go stale
before any of them, and it never established the read would succeed.

Same fix view.ts already carries for this rule (#389): read straight out
and let ENOENT mean absent, so there is no window between the check and
the use.

Narrowing to ENOENT is the part that matters. Collapsing every read
error into "absent" sends a config we merely failed to read down the
mkdir-and-write branch, which replaces it and leaves no `.bak` — the
copy only runs on the branch that read something.

The new test pins that: a write-only config (read fails, write would
succeed) must surface EACCES with the user's content intact. It fails
against the collapsed-catch mutant and passes here. The earlier shape of
this test used a directory, which throws EISDIR either way and proved
nothing.

801 tests pass; knip, typecheck and lint clean.
